newsitem.title: JAPAN: JAPAN DEPT STORE SALES SEEN FALLING IN JULY--PAPER.
newsitem.headline: JAPAN DEPT STORE SALES SEEN FALLING IN JULY--PAPER.

text.p: Sales at department stores in Tokyo and Osaka in July are expected to have been less than in the same month last year, the Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said over the weekend.
It would be the fourth consecutive month of year-on-year declines, it said.
The expected fall in July is due to a reaction to an increase in sales tax on April 1 and the cancellation of a special tax break, the paper said.
Purchase by corporate customers and purchase of gift items were slow in July, it added.
It is unlikely that department store sales will pick up in August, the paper said, adding that sluggish consumer spending is likely to continue for some time.
